text: A pre-2.19.0 project is refused with the two-hop instruction named. **CLOSED SAME DAY: found unsatisfied 2026-08-17 (vc), fixed by cc at `f2b7b97a`, re-measured satisfied by vc against the same estate -- `intent upgrade` on pinned Utilz now exits 1 naming `2.18.0`, the `v2.19.0` floor and `install intent@2`, writes nothing (101/101 verified, stamp untouched), while the 2.19.0 canary still converts.** The fix is one arm before `legacy::scan` -- refuse iff `Pending { below_floor: true }`, remedy delegated to `Pending::remedy()` rather than copied -- and a distinct `BelowMigrationFloor` variant rather than reusing `Unmigrated`, because both carry the same data and **the operator's situation differs**: _this project has not been migrated_ is news to someone who asked a question and a restatement of their own intent to someone who just ran the migrator. The record of the original finding follows, because how it was found is the reusable part. **MEASURED UNSATISFIED 2026-08-17 (vc), against the only real pre-2.19.0 estate in the fleet corpus: Utilz declares `2.18.0` and `Facade::upgrade` MIGRATED it** -- 61 files, 9 threads, 19 carried findings, no refusal, and `config.json` left reading `3.0.0-dev`. **The mechanism is a floor enforced on the door that READS and not on the door that WRITES**: `Facade::open` calls `Self::readable()`, which returns `FacadeError::Unmigrated(pending)` whose `remedy()` is delegated precisely so the sub-floor case gets the two-hop (`facade.rs:406` says so); `Facade::upgrade` never calls `readable()` and goes straight to `legacy::scan`. **Why it is worse than a missing guard: the two-hop exists because 2.19.0 is where the AT row grammar landed**, so a 2.18.0 estate migrated straight to v3 skips that migration and its AT rows arrive in a grammar v3 was never told about, silently, because nothing on this path is looking. AT-10.1 (`migrate_floor.rs`) is `to-write`, so this is an unbuilt criterion with a measurement attached rather than a regression. **It could only have been found by a real sub-floor estate** -- the canary and Lamplight and Baize all declare 2.19.0, and a constructed fixture would have been built by someone who already knew the floor was the question
